title: basic-auth model-version create: READ on the source run or logged model must be checked on proto-bound ids so camelCase runId/modelId aliases cannot bypass it
answers: Why could a user register a model version from a run they cannot read in basic-auth, and then download its artifacts?
Does the model version create endpoint accept runId or modelId in camelCase, and is the source-read check applied to them?
Creating a model version from a nonexistent run or logged model returns 404 instead of 403 in basic auth, is that expected?
Where is the READ permission on the source run checked when a model version is created?
body:
Path: POST /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/create (create model version from a run or logged model) passes through the basic-auth validator `mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_create_model_version`, which gates registered-model UPDATE and then the READ check on the referenced source run or logged model.
Rule: The validator parses the body through the proto with `_get_request_message(CreateModelVersion())`, so the snake_case `run_id`/`model_id` and camelCase `runId`/`modelId` keys are all bound. It uses `msg.HasField(...)` for presence, then authorizes the bound value via `_get_run_permission` / `_get_model_permission` wrapped in `_can_read_model_version_source`, which maps RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST to a denial.
Symptom: A body carrying only `runId` (or `modelId`) skipped the source READ check, because the validator only looked for the snake_case keys. The handler still anchored the new version to that run or logged model, so a user with no READ on another user's run could read its artifacts through a registered model they created.
Constraints: An explicitly empty id is still denied (presence via HasField, then truthiness). A nonexistent id is denied with 403 rather than the store's 404, to avoid an existence oracle. A non-dict body degrades to an empty message and falls through to the handler's own validation. Applies to the basic-auth app only.
Applies: Basic-auth authorization for model version creation from a source run or logged model, including any new source-id alias on this request.
applies: Basic-auth validator for CreateModelVersion requests in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py.
says: Users can register a model version from private runs and download artifacts they cannot access.
Block registering model versions when the user lacks view permissions on the source run.
Prevent unauthorized members from stealing model artifacts by creating registered versions from restricted experiments.
Registering a model version from a nonexistent run should return permission denied not missing.
search: For basic-auth model version creation, validate_can_create_model_version parses the request body using _get_request_message(CreateModelVersion()) and checks HasField to ensure both snake_case and camelCase run and model identifiers enforce source read authorization. This prevents requests containing only camelCase runId or modelId from bypassing read checks on source runs or logged models while still registering versions and exposing artifacts. The check maps RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST to a 403 denial rather than a 404 to prevent existence oracles, denies explicitly empty identifiers, and falls through on non-dict bodies. This applies strictly to the basic-auth CreateModelVersion endpoint in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py and any new source identifier aliases.
